# OpenAgents CLI: local inference commands and teach status

- Class: owner-accepted CLI and teach-mode contract
- Status: accepted 2026-08-29; implementation not started
- Intent: [INTENT.md](./INTENT.md)
- Plan: [PLAN.md](./PLAN.md)
- Bytes behind the statuses: [LLAMA_CPP_INFERENCE_PIPELINE.md](./LLAMA_CPP_INFERENCE_PIPELINE.md)

This document is the command surface people type, the order we build it,
and the **exact status lines** the terminal shows from first GGUF lookup
through a finished generation. Implementation fills those lines in from
the top. It does not spawn `llama-server`. It does not call Ollama.

```text
CLAIM
actor/session: psionic CLI teach-status contract
base: 43d471cc56f6ea8e0db434762be19019df7dec0f
worktree/branch: psionic-cli-docs / detached github/main
scope: CLI commands, teach mode, canonical status script, build order
paths: docs/psionic/CLI.md and cross-links in docs/psionic/
hot files: none
hot contracts: none
verification: docs-only; whitespace and path-local review
claimed_at: 2026-08-29T16:20:00Z
```

## How you watch the work

The spine command is `openagents inference run`. While this program is
under construction, that command defaults to **teach mode**: every
canonical status line prints as it happens, and any step that is not in
the binary yet prints as not built, then the process stops.

You do not wait for Coder before you can see load progress. You run
`inference run` against a GGUF path. Each merged slice lights up more of
the same script until the last line is `Inference complete`.

`--preview` prints the whole script without opening a file. Use it to
read the map. `--until <step-id>` runs only through that step.

## Commands

Two root subcommands join the existing `Commands` enum in
`crates/openagents-cli/src/cli.rs`. Global flags already on the binary
still apply: `--json`, `--verbose`, `--no-color`.

Teach status goes to stderr as text. `--json` emits the same steps as
one JSON object per line on stderr (`id`, `message`, `state`, fields).
Stdout stays for the generation (token text) or a final summary.

### `openagents inference`

Product lifecycle and the visible run loop. No training. No mesh.

| Command | What you do with it |
| --- | --- |
| `inference run` | Walk the load-and-generate path in this process. First command to implement. Teach mode default. |
| `inference models` | List admitted GGUFs in the local store. |
| `inference add <path-or-ref>` | Admit a GGUF, copy it into `~/.openagents/inference/models/<digest>.gguf`, write a manifest. Downloads only for an allowlisted ref with an expected digest. |
| `inference remove <model>` | Delete a store entry. |
| `inference serve` | Same load path, then bind OpenAI-compatible HTTP on `127.0.0.1`. Refuse `0.0.0.0` by default. Optional for first Coder green. |
| `inference status` | Show whether a `serve` child of this CLI is loaded, which model, backend, digest. |
| `inference stop` | Stop that `serve`. An in-process Coder turn does not use this. |
| `inference doctor` | Backends, store path, last admitted model, Metal/CPU presence. |

`run` flags:

```text
openagents inference run
  --gguf <path>              Local GGUF (required until the store has a default)
  --model <id>               Admitted store id (later)
  --prompt <text>            Prompt for tokenize and generate steps
  --max-tokens <n>           Decode budget (generate steps)
  --backend auto|metal|cpu   Default auto
  --teach / --no-teach       Teach is default on run until Coder is the product path
  --quiet                    One line per phase, no teach explanations
  --preview                  Print the full status script; do not open a GGUF
  --until <step-id>          Stop after this step succeeds
```

`--verbose` (global) adds debug logs. It does not replace `--teach`.
Teach is the stable, user-facing script. Verbose is for developers
grepping library internals.

### `openagents psionic`

Harness. Use this when you are probing the library rather than running
the product loop.

| Command | What you do with it |
| --- | --- |
| `psionic inspect <artifact>` | Dump GGUF architecture, tensor names, sizes. No mmap of weights required. |
| `psionic admit <artifact>` | Run admission only: family, digest, required tensors, refuse unknown. |
| `psionic backends` | List compiled backends. |
| `psionic doctor` | Library graph, feature flags, provenance pin. |

`inspect` and `admit` share the early GGUF steps with `inference run`.
They stop before mmap. Prefer `inference run --until meta.done` when you
want the same messages the product command will keep.

### `openagents coder`

Unchanged until stage 4 in [PLAN.md](./PLAN.md). Then
`--model psionic:<id>` uses the same in-process path as `inference run`,
without teach lines in the TUI unless you opt in. Ollama stays on
`ollama:` until replacement gates pass.

## Build order

Implement from the top of the status script. Each slice is a CLI you can
run. Later slices keep the earlier messages.

| Slice | `--until` | Commands that become useful | Exit when the slice is done |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `script` | `inference run --preview` | Prints every canonical line as `pending`. No file I/O. |
| 1 | `gguf.found` | `inference run --gguf <path>` | Locates a local file. No parse. |
| 2 | `gguf.open` | same | Opens the fd. Reads magic and version. |
| 3 | `meta.done` | `run`, `psionic inspect` | KV metadata and tensor index. Architecture, shapes, quant. Still no weight mmap. |
| 4 | `tok.done` | `run --prompt …` (tokenize only) | Vocab and BPE merges from GGUF KV. |
| 5 | `admit.done` | `psionic admit`, `inference add` | Required `qwen35` names (and Ollama `mtp.*` rename if needed). Store copy. |
| 6 | `map.done` | `run` | mmap, named tensors, CPU vs Metal placement, shared Metal buffer, `data` pointers. |
| 7 | `ctx.done` | `run` | Context, hybrid KV and Gated DeltaNet caches, scheduler. |
| 8 | `prompt.done` | `run --prompt` | Chat template and tokenize. |
| 9 | `prefill.done` | `run --prompt` | Prefill all prompt positions. |
| 10 | `gen.done` | `run --prompt --max-tokens` | Decode, sample, stream, stop. **Inference complete.** |
| 11 | (product) | `models`, `serve`, `doctor`, Coder | Lifecycle around the same path. |

Slice 1 is the first code packet after provenance. It prints `Looking
for GGUF` through `Found GGUF at …`. Slice 3 is the first packet that
proves we parsed a real file. Slice 10 is the first token out.

Do not skip ahead to generate while `meta.done` is missing. Do not hide
a missing step by calling Ollama.

## Teach output

Each step has a stable `id` (for `--until`, `--json`, and tests) and a
**message** (what you read).

Text form, teach default:

```text
[gguf.look] Looking for GGUF
            Checking the model store and any --gguf path you passed.
```

`state` is `ok`, `pending`, `skip`, or `fail`.

- `ok` — this process just did the step. Fill `{placeholders}`.
- `pending` — `--preview`, or a later slice not in the binary. Message
  stays in the canonical wording with placeholders not filled.
- `skip` — step does not apply (no download if the file is already
  local).
- `fail` — stop. Print the fail message. Non-zero exit.

After the last `ok` step, if the next canonical step is not built and
you did not pass `--until` at the last `ok`:

```text
[build.stop] Stopping: next step is not built yet
             Last completed step: meta.done
             Next to build: tok.read
```

`--until` on a built step exits 0 after that step without printing the
rest as pending, unless `--teach` and `--preview` are both set.

## Canonical status script

This is the entire path. Placeholders in `{braces}` are replaced on
`ok`. Quoted messages are the user-visible strings. Do not rephrase them
in code.

Download lines run only when `add` / `run` is given an allowlisted remote
ref and the digest is not already in the store. Otherwise those ids emit
`skip`.

### Slice 0 — script

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `run.start` | `Starting inference run` |
| `run.teach` | `Teach mode on` |
| `run.until` | `Running until {step-id}` |
| `run.preview` | `Preview only; not opening a GGUF` |

### Slice 1 — find the file

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `gguf.look` | `Looking for GGUF` |
| `gguf.store` | `Checking model store at {store-path}` |
| `gguf.path` | `Checking local path {path}` |
| `gguf.missing` | `GGUF not in store` |
| `gguf.download` | `Downloading GGUF from {source} to {dest}` |
| `gguf.download.progress` | `Download progress {bytes}/{total} bytes` |
| `gguf.download.done` | `Download complete` |
| `gguf.hash` | `Verifying SHA-256` |
| `gguf.hash.ok` | `Digest matches {digest}` |
| `gguf.found` | `Found GGUF at {path} ({size})` |

First implementation target: `gguf.look`, `gguf.path`, `gguf.found` for
`--gguf`. Store, download, and hash wait for `inference add` / allowlist
work in slice 5. Until then, if there is no `--gguf`, fail with
`Looking for GGUF` then `No GGUF path given; pass --gguf`.

Fail messages (same id family, `state=fail`):

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `gguf.fail.arg` | `No GGUF path given; pass --gguf` |
| `gguf.fail.missing` | `GGUF not found at {path}` |
| `gguf.fail.hash` | `Digest mismatch: expected {expected}, got {got}` |

### Slice 2 — open header

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `gguf.open` | `Opening GGUF {path}` |
| `gguf.load` | `Loading GGUF` |
| `gguf.magic` | `Reading magic` |
| `gguf.magic.ok` | `Magic is GGUF` |
| `gguf.version` | `Reading version` |
| `gguf.version.ok` | `Version is {version}` |

| id | Fail message |
| --- | --- |
| `gguf.fail.magic` | `Not a GGUF file (magic is {got})` |
| `gguf.fail.version` | `Unsupported GGUF version {version}` |

### Slice 3 — metadata and tensor index

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `gguf.n_tensors` | `Reading tensor count` |
| `gguf.n_tensors.ok` | `Tensor count is {n}` |
| `gguf.n_kv` | `Reading key-value count` |
| `gguf.n_kv.ok` | `Key-value count is {n}` |
| `meta.read` | `Reading metadata` |
| `meta.arch` | `Architecture is {arch}` |
| `meta.ftype` | `File type is {ftype}` |
| `meta.embd` | `Hidden width is {n}` |
| `meta.layers` | `Layer count is {n}` |
| `meta.vocab` | `Vocabulary size is {n}` |
| `meta.ffn` | `FFN width is {n}` |
| `meta.quant` | `Quantization is {quant}` |
| `meta.attn_interval` | `Full-attention interval is {n}` |
| `meta.nextn` | `MTP extra layers is {n}` |
| `meta.ctx` | `Trained context length is {n}` |
| `idx.read` | `Reading tensor index` |
| `idx.ok` | `Indexed {n} tensors` |
| `meta.done` | `Metadata ready` |

| id | Fail message |
| --- | --- |
| `meta.fail.arch` | `Unsupported architecture {arch}` |
| `idx.fail` | `Tensor index is truncated or corrupt` |

This slice is parse-only (`no_alloc`). It does not map weights.

### Slice 4 — tokenizer tables (still KV, not weights)

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `tok.read` | `Reading tokenizer` |
| `tok.model` | `Tokenizer model is {model}` |
| `tok.tokens` | `Loaded {n} tokens` |
| `tok.merges` | `Loaded {n} BPE merges` |
| `tok.special` | `Special tokens bos={bos} eos={eos}` |
| `tok.done` | `Tokenizer ready` |

| id | Fail message |
| --- | --- |
| `tok.fail.model` | `Unsupported tokenizer model {model}` |
| `tok.fail.merges` | `Tokenizer merges missing` |

### Slice 5 — admit and store

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `name.translate` | `Translating Ollama tensor names to llama.cpp names` |
| `name.check` | `Checking required tensor names` |
| `admit.ok` | `Admission passed for {family} digest {digest}` |
| `store.copy` | `Copying GGUF into store {dest}` |
| `store.manifest` | `Wrote manifest {path}` |
| `admit.done` | `Model admitted` |

`name.translate` is `skip` when names are already `blk.N.nextn.*`.

| id | Fail message |
| --- | --- |
| `admit.fail.tensor` | `Missing required tensor {name}` |
| `admit.fail.family` | `Refusing to alias {arch} as a different family` |

### Slice 6 — mmap and Metal (weights)

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `backend.load` | `Loading backends` |
| `backend.cpu` | `CPU backend ready` |
| `backend.metal` | `Metal backend ready` |
| `backend.pick` | `Selected backend is {backend}` |
| `map.mmap` | `Mapping GGUF into memory` |
| `map.mmap.ok` | `mmap size {size}` |
| `map.tensors` | `Creating named tensors` |
| `map.devices` | `Assigning devices: embeddings on CPU, {n_layers} layers on {backend}, output on {backend}` |
| `map.metal` | `Wrapping mmap as Metal shared buffer` |
| `map.bind` | `Binding tensor data pointers` |
| `map.unmap` | `Unmapping unused header and tail` |
| `map.done` | `Weights ready ({size} mapped)` |

`map.metal` is `skip` on CPU-only. Fail if Metal was requested and the
shared wrap cannot be created; do not fall back to Ollama.

| id | Fail message |
| --- | --- |
| `backend.fail` | `No usable backend ({reason})` |
| `map.fail.mmap` | `mmap failed: {reason}` |
| `map.fail.metal` | `Metal shared buffer failed: {reason}` |

### Slice 7 — context and caches

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `ctx.alloc` | `Allocating context` |
| `ctx.length` | `Context length is {n}` |
| `ctx.kv` | `Allocating KV cache for {n} full-attention layers` |
| `ctx.gdn` | `Allocating recurrent state for {n} Gated DeltaNet layers` |
| `ctx.sched` | `Graph scheduler ready` |
| `ctx.done` | `Context ready` |

| id | Fail message |
| --- | --- |
| `ctx.fail.mem` | `Not enough memory for context {n}: {reason}` |

### Slice 8 — prompt

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `prompt.template` | `Applying chat template` |
| `prompt.tokenize` | `Tokenizing prompt` |
| `prompt.done` | `Prompt is {n} tokens` |

| id | Fail message |
| --- | --- |
| `prompt.fail.empty` | `No prompt given; pass --prompt` |
| `prompt.fail.tok` | `Tokenize failed: {reason}` |

### Slice 9 — prefill

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `prefill.start` | `Prefill starting` |
| `prefill.pos` | `Prefill position {i}/{n}` |
| `prefill.done` | `Prefill complete` |

`prefill.pos` may throttle (for example every 32 positions plus last)
so a long prompt does not flood the terminal. `--teach` still shows
start and complete. `--json` may emit every position.

### Slice 10 — generate

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `gen.step` | `Decode step {i}` |
| `gen.logits` | `Computing logits` |
| `gen.sample` | `Sampling token {id} ({piece})` |
| `gen.stream` | `Streaming {piece}` |
| `gen.stop.eos` | `Stop: end of sequence` |
| `gen.stop.length` | `Stop: token budget {n}` |
| `gen.stop.cancel` | `Stop: cancelled` |
| `gen.stats` | `Generated {n} tokens` |
| `gen.done` | `Inference complete` |

Token pieces also write to stdout as they stream (product path). Teach
lines on stderr stay in sync with that stream.

## Example: first slice you can run

When only slice 1 exists:

```text
$ openagents inference run --gguf /models/qwen38.gguf --until gguf.found
[run.start] Starting inference run
[run.teach] Teach mode on
[run.until] Running until gguf.found
[gguf.look] Looking for GGUF
[gguf.path] Checking local path /models/qwen38.gguf
[gguf.found] Found GGUF at /models/qwen38.gguf (29.1 GiB)
```

When slices 1–3 exist and you omit `--until`:

```text
… metadata lines …
[meta.done] Metadata ready
[build.stop] Stopping: next step is not built yet
             Last completed step: meta.done
             Next to build: tok.read
```

`--preview` (works in slice 0):

```text
$ openagents inference run --preview
[run.preview] Preview only; not opening a GGUF
[gguf.look] Looking for GGUF                          pending
[gguf.store] Checking model store at {store-path}     pending
…
[gen.done] Inference complete                         pending
```

## JSON lines

With `--json`, each step is one object:

```text
{"id":"gguf.look","message":"Looking for GGUF","state":"ok"}
{"id":"gguf.found","message":"Found GGUF at /models/qwen38.gguf (29.1 GiB)","state":"ok","path":"/models/qwen38.gguf","size":31226560320}
```

Tests assert `id` and `state`, not wrapping prose.

## Relation to other docs

[PLAN.md](./PLAN.md) still owns crate allowlist, Coder stages, and
replacement gates. This file owns the strings people see and the
`--until` ladder.

[LLAMA_CPP_INFERENCE_PIPELINE.md](./LLAMA_CPP_INFERENCE_PIPELINE.md)
owns mmap, Metal `newBufferWithBytesNoCopy`, Q8_0 blocks, and the
`qwen35` graph. Teach messages are the human labels for those steps.

[QWEN38_INFERENCE_PIPELINE.md](./QWEN38_INFERENCE_PIPELINE.md) owns the
decoder math. CLI statuses do not replace that document.

Weights stay out of git. `run --gguf` reads a path you already have.
`add` is what puts a copy under `~/.openagents/inference/`.

| `inference status` | Show whether a `serve` child of this CLI is loaded, which model, backend, digest. |
| `inference stop` | Stop that `serve`. An in-process Coder turn does not use this. |
| `inference doctor` | Backends, store path, last admitted model, Metal/CPU presence. |

`run` flags:

```text
openagents inference run
  --gguf <path>              Local GGUF (required until the store has a default)
  --model <id>               Admitted store id (later)
  --prompt <text>            Prompt for tokenize and generate steps
  --max-tokens <n>           Decode budget (generate steps)
  --backend auto|metal|cpu   Default auto
  --teach / --no-teach       Teach is default on run until Coder is the product path
  --quiet                    One line per phase, no teach explanations
  --preview                  Print the full status script; do not open a GGUF
  --until <step-id>          Stop after this step succeeds
```

`--verbose` (global) adds debug logs. It does not replace `--teach`.
Teach is the stable, user-facing script. Verbose is for developers
grepping library internals.

### `openagents psionic`

Harness. Use this when you are probing the library rather than running
the product loop.

| Command | What you do with it |
| --- | --- |
| `psionic inspect <artifact>` | Dump GGUF architecture, tensor names, sizes. No mmap of weights required. |
| `psionic admit <artifact>` | Run admission only: family, digest, required tensors, refuse unknown. |
| `psionic backends` | List compiled backends. |
| `psionic doctor` | Library graph, feature flags, provenance pin. |

`inspect` and `admit` share the early GGUF steps with `inference run`.
They stop before mmap. Prefer `inference run --until meta.done` when you
want the same messages the product command will keep.

### `openagents coder`

Unchanged until stage 4 in [PLAN.md](./PLAN.md). Then
`--model psionic:<id>` uses the same in-process path as `inference run`,
without teach lines in the TUI unless you opt in. Ollama stays on
`ollama:` until replacement gates pass.

## Build order

Implement from the top of the status script. Each slice is a CLI you can
run. Later slices keep the earlier messages.

| Slice | `--until` | Commands that become useful | Exit when the slice is done |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `script` | `inference run --preview` | Prints every canonical line as `pending`. No file I/O. |
| 1 | `gguf.found` | `inference run --gguf <path>` | Locates a local file. No parse. |
| 2 | `gguf.open` | same | Opens the fd. Reads magic and version. |
| 3 | `meta.done` | `run`, `psionic inspect` | KV metadata and tensor index. Architecture, shapes, quant. Still no weight mmap. |
| 4 | `tok.done` | `run --prompt …` (tokenize only) | Vocab and BPE merges from GGUF KV. |
| 5 | `admit.done` | `psionic admit`, `inference add` | Required `qwen35` names (and Ollama `mtp.*` rename if needed). Store copy. |
| 6 | `map.done` | `run` | mmap, named tensors, CPU vs Metal placement, shared Metal buffer, `data` pointers. |
| 7 | `ctx.done` | `run` | Context, hybrid KV and Gated DeltaNet caches, scheduler. |
| 8 | `prompt.done` | `run --prompt` | Chat template and tokenize. |
| 9 | `prefill.done` | `run --prompt` | Prefill all prompt positions. |
| 10 | `gen.done` | `run --prompt --max-tokens` | Decode, sample, stream, stop. **Inference complete.** |
| 11 | (product) | `models`, `serve`, `doctor`, Coder | Lifecycle around the same path. |

Slice 1 is the first code packet after provenance. It prints `Looking
for GGUF` through `Found GGUF at …`. Slice 3 is the first packet that
proves we parsed a real file. Slice 10 is the first token out.

Do not skip ahead to generate while `meta.done` is missing. Do not hide
a missing step by calling Ollama.

## Teach output

Each step has a stable `id` (for `--until`, `--json`, and tests) and a
**message** (what you read).

Text form, teach default:

```text
[gguf.look] Looking for GGUF
            Checking the model store and any --gguf path you passed.
```

`state` is `ok`, `pending`, `skip`, or `fail`.

- `ok` — this process just did the step. Fill `{placeholders}`.
- `pending` — `--preview`, or a later slice not in the binary. Message
  stays in the canonical wording with placeholders not filled.
- `skip` — step does not apply (no download if the file is already
  local).
- `fail` — stop. Print the fail message. Non-zero exit.

After the last `ok` step, if the next canonical step is not built and
you did not pass `--until` at the last `ok`:

```text
[build.stop] Stopping: next step is not built yet
             Last completed step: meta.done
             Next to build: tok.read
```

`--until` on a built step exits 0 after that step without printing the
rest as pending, unless `--teach` and `--preview` are both set.

## Canonical status script

This is the entire path. Placeholders in `{braces}` are replaced on
`ok`. Quoted messages are the user-visible strings. Do not rephrase them
in code.

Download lines run only when `add` / `run` is given an allowlisted remote
ref and the digest is not already in the store. Otherwise those ids emit
`skip`.

### Slice 0 — script

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `run.start` | `Starting inference run` |
| `run.teach` | `Teach mode on` |
| `run.until` | `Running until {step-id}` |
| `run.preview` | `Preview only; not opening a GGUF` |

### Slice 1 — find the file

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `gguf.look` | `Looking for GGUF` |
| `gguf.store` | `Checking model store at {store-path}` |
| `gguf.path` | `Checking local path {path}` |
| `gguf.missing` | `GGUF not in store` |
| `gguf.download` | `Downloading GGUF from {source} to {dest}` |
| `gguf.download.progress` | `Download progress {bytes}/{total} bytes` |
| `gguf.download.done` | `Download complete` |
| `gguf.hash` | `Verifying SHA-256` |
| `gguf.hash.ok` | `Digest matches {digest}` |
| `gguf.found` | `Found GGUF at {path} ({size})` |

First implementation target: `gguf.look`, `gguf.path`, `gguf.found` for
`--gguf`. Store, download, and hash wait for `inference add` / allowlist
work in slice 5. Until then, if there is no `--gguf`, fail with
`Looking for GGUF` then `No GGUF path given; pass --gguf`.

Fail messages (same id family, `state=fail`):

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `gguf.fail.arg` | `No GGUF path given; pass --gguf` |
| `gguf.fail.missing` | `GGUF not found at {path}` |
| `gguf.fail.hash` | `Digest mismatch: expected {expected}, got {got}` |

### Slice 2 — open header

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `gguf.open` | `Opening GGUF {path}` |
| `gguf.load` | `Loading GGUF` |
| `gguf.magic` | `Reading magic` |
| `gguf.magic.ok` | `Magic is GGUF` |
| `gguf.version` | `Reading version` |
| `gguf.version.ok` | `Version is {version}` |

| id | Fail message |
| --- | --- |
| `gguf.fail.magic` | `Not a GGUF file (magic is {got})` |
| `gguf.fail.version` | `Unsupported GGUF version {version}` |

### Slice 3 — metadata and tensor index

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `gguf.n_tensors` | `Reading tensor count` |
| `gguf.n_tensors.ok` | `Tensor count is {n}` |
| `gguf.n_kv` | `Reading key-value count` |
| `gguf.n_kv.ok` | `Key-value count is {n}` |
| `meta.read` | `Reading metadata` |
| `meta.arch` | `Architecture is {arch}` |
| `meta.ftype` | `File type is {ftype}` |
| `meta.embd` | `Hidden width is {n}` |
| `meta.layers` | `Layer count is {n}` |
| `meta.vocab` | `Vocabulary size is {n}` |
| `meta.ffn` | `FFN width is {n}` |
| `meta.quant` | `Quantization is {quant}` |
| `meta.attn_interval` | `Full-attention interval is {n}` |
| `meta.nextn` | `MTP extra layers is {n}` |
| `meta.ctx` | `Trained context length is {n}` |
| `idx.read` | `Reading tensor index` |
| `idx.ok` | `Indexed {n} tensors` |
| `meta.done` | `Metadata ready` |

| id | Fail message |
| --- | --- |
| `meta.fail.arch` | `Unsupported architecture {arch}` |
| `idx.fail` | `Tensor index is truncated or corrupt` |

This slice is parse-only (`no_alloc`). It does not map weights.

### Slice 4 — tokenizer tables (still KV, not weights)

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `tok.read` | `Reading tokenizer` |
| `tok.model` | `Tokenizer model is {model}` |
| `tok.tokens` | `Loaded {n} tokens` |
| `tok.merges` | `Loaded {n} BPE merges` |
| `tok.special` | `Special tokens bos={bos} eos={eos}` |
| `tok.done` | `Tokenizer ready` |

| id | Fail message |
| --- | --- |
| `tok.fail.model` | `Unsupported tokenizer model {model}` |
| `tok.fail.merges` | `Tokenizer merges missing` |

### Slice 5 — admit and store

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `name.translate` | `Translating Ollama tensor names to llama.cpp names` |
| `name.check` | `Checking required tensor names` |
| `admit.ok` | `Admission passed for {family} digest {digest}` |
| `store.copy` | `Copying GGUF into store {dest}` |
| `store.manifest` | `Wrote manifest {path}` |
| `admit.done` | `Model admitted` |

`name.translate` is `skip` when names are already `blk.N.nextn.*`.

| id | Fail message |
| --- | --- |
| `admit.fail.tensor` | `Missing required tensor {name}` |
| `admit.fail.family` | `Refusing to alias {arch} as a different family` |

### Slice 6 — mmap and Metal (weights)

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `backend.load` | `Loading backends` |
| `backend.cpu` | `CPU backend ready` |
| `backend.metal` | `Metal backend ready` |
| `backend.pick` | `Selected backend is {backend}` |
| `map.mmap` | `Mapping GGUF into memory` |
| `map.mmap.ok` | `mmap size {size}` |
| `map.tensors` | `Creating named tensors` |
| `map.devices` | `Assigning devices: embeddings on CPU, {n_layers} layers on {backend}, output on {backend}` |
| `map.metal` | `Wrapping mmap as Metal shared buffer` |
| `map.bind` | `Binding tensor data pointers` |
| `map.unmap` | `Unmapping unused header and tail` |
| `map.done` | `Weights ready ({size} mapped)` |

`map.metal` is `skip` on CPU-only. Fail if Metal was requested and the
shared wrap cannot be created; do not fall back to Ollama.

| id | Fail message |
| --- | --- |
| `backend.fail` | `No usable backend ({reason})` |
| `map.fail.mmap` | `mmap failed: {reason}` |
| `map.fail.metal` | `Metal shared buffer failed: {reason}` |

### Slice 7 — context and caches

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `ctx.alloc` | `Allocating context` |
| `ctx.length` | `Context length is {n}` |
| `ctx.kv` | `Allocating KV cache for {n} full-attention layers` |
| `ctx.gdn` | `Allocating recurrent state for {n} Gated DeltaNet layers` |
| `ctx.sched` | `Graph scheduler ready` |
| `ctx.done` | `Context ready` |

| id | Fail message |
| --- | --- |
| `ctx.fail.mem` | `Not enough memory for context {n}: {reason}` |

### Slice 8 — prompt

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `prompt.template` | `Applying chat template` |
| `prompt.tokenize` | `Tokenizing prompt` |
| `prompt.done` | `Prompt is {n} tokens` |

| id | Fail message |
| --- | --- |
| `prompt.fail.empty` | `No prompt given; pass --prompt` |
| `prompt.fail.tok` | `Tokenize failed: {reason}` |

### Slice 9 — prefill

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `prefill.start` | `Prefill starting` |
| `prefill.pos` | `Prefill position {i}/{n}` |
| `prefill.done` | `Prefill complete` |

`prefill.pos` may throttle (for example every 32 positions plus last)
so a long prompt does not flood the terminal. `--teach` still shows
start and complete. `--json` may emit every position.

### Slice 10 — generate

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `gen.step` | `Decode step {i}` |
| `gen.logits` | `Computing logits` |
| `gen.sample` | `Sampling token {id} ({piece})` |
| `gen.stream` | `Streaming {piece}` |
| `gen.stop.eos` | `Stop: end of sequence` |
| `gen.stop.length` | `Stop: token budget {n}` |
| `gen.stop.cancel` | `Stop: cancelled` |
| `gen.stats` | `Generated {n} tokens` |
| `gen.done` | `Inference complete` |

Token pieces also write to stdout as they stream (product path). Teach
lines on stderr stay in sync with that stream.

## Example: first slice you can run

When only slice 1 exists:

```text
$ openagents inference run --gguf /models/qwen38.gguf --until gguf.found
[run.start] Starting inference run
[run.teach] Teach mode on
[run.until] Running until gguf.found
[gguf.look] Looking for GGUF
[gguf.path] Checking local path /models/qwen38.gguf
[gguf.found] Found GGUF at /models/qwen38.gguf (29.1 GiB)
```

When slices 1–3 exist and you omit `--until`:

```text
… metadata lines …
[meta.done] Metadata ready
[build.stop] Stopping: next step is not built yet
             Last completed step: meta.done
             Next to build: tok.read
```

`--preview` (works in slice 0):

```text
$ openagents inference run --preview
[run.preview] Preview only; not opening a GGUF
[gguf.look] Looking for GGUF                          pending
[gguf.store] Checking model store at {store-path}     pending
…
[gen.done] Inference complete                         pending
```

## JSON lines

With `--json`, each step is one object:

```text
{"id":"gguf.look","message":"Looking for GGUF","state":"ok"}
{"id":"gguf.found","message":"Found GGUF at /models/qwen38.gguf (29.1 GiB)","state":"ok","path":"/models/qwen38.gguf","size":31226560320}
```

Tests assert `id` and `state`, not wrapping prose.

## Relation to other docs

[PLAN.md](./PLAN.md) still owns crate allowlist, Coder stages, and
replacement gates. This file owns the strings people see and the
`--until` ladder.

[LLAMA_CPP_INFERENCE_PIPELINE.md](./LLAMA_CPP_INFERENCE_PIPELINE.md)
owns mmap, Metal `newBufferWithBytesNoCopy`, Q8_0 blocks, and the
`qwen35` graph. Teach messages are the human labels for those steps.

[QWEN38_INFERENCE_PIPELINE.md](./QWEN38_INFERENCE_PIPELINE.md) owns the
decoder math. CLI statuses do not replace that document.

Weights stay out of git. `run --gguf` reads a path you already have.
`add` is what puts a copy under `~/.openagents/inference/`.

## CLI surface

Normative command list, teach mode, `--until` ladder, and the exact
status strings are [CLI.md](./CLI.md). This section is the summary.

Add two root commands next to the existing `Commands` enum in
`crates/openagents-cli/src/cli.rs`.

### `openagents inference`

Product lifecycle and the visible in-process loop. No training. No mesh.

```text
openagents inference run [--gguf <path>] [--prompt <text>] [--until <step>] [--preview]
openagents inference models
openagents inference add <path-or-approved-ref>
openagents inference remove <model>
openagents inference serve [--model <id>] [--backend auto|metal|cpu|cuda] [--port <n>]
openagents inference status
openagents inference stop
openagents inference doctor
```

`run` is the first command to implement. It prints the canonical status
script (Looking for GGUF, Loading GGUF, Reading metadata, … through
Inference complete). Teach mode is the default on `run` until Coder is
the product path. Each slice implements the next `--until` step. A step
that is not in the binary prints as not built and stops.

`add` inspects with the imported GGUF admission code, writes a manifest
(digest, family, backend list, license ack), and copies into the model
store. It does not download unless the reference is on an allowlist with
an expected digest.

`serve` loads the admitted artifact on the chosen backend and binds
`127.0.0.1`. Default refuse `0.0.0.0`. Coder does not have to use this
HTTP port; the same load path is a Rust API.

`stop` applies to a background serve started by this command. An
in-process Coder turn does not need a separate daemon.

### 0. This folder

### 1. Provenance and compile graph

Pin a Psionic revision. List every crate that must copy for a Qwen 3.8 CPU
fixture to compile. Write `PROVENANCE.md`. CLI may land a `--preview`
stub that prints pending statuses with no library yet.

Copy the allowlisted crates. Implement `openagents inference run --gguf`
through `--until meta.done` (Looking for GGUF → Loading GGUF → Reading
metadata → tensor index). `openagents psionic inspect` and `admit` on a
fixture GGUF. Tests: malformed GGUF refuses; admitted fixture reports
family and digest.

**Exit:** fixture admission is deterministic in CI. `run --until
meta.done` prints the canonical statuses on a fixture file.

### 3. `openagents inference` + in-process generate

Tokenizer, mmap/Metal, context, prefill, decode (`--until gen.done`).
Model store, `add`/`models`/`doctor`. Optional loopback `serve` if it is
cheaper than a second API.

**Exit:** `openagents inference run --prompt …` prints `Inference
complete` on the fixture. `openagents inference doctor` is green on a
machine with the fixture.

## Outcome

`openagents inference run --gguf <path> --until map.done` walks the in-process path from GGUF lookup through mmap and Metal wrap and prints `Weights ready`. Teach strings and `--json` ids stay exactly as in `docs/psionic/CLI.md`. No `llama-server`. No Ollama.

Generate (`gen.done`), Coder `--model psionic:`, default `--local` flip, unloading, memory meters, 27B laptop receipt.

## Outcome

Loaded weights can leave the process. mmap, Metal shared buffer, and named tensors are released. The CLI and Coder both expose that action. After unload, a later load starts from Looking for GGUF again.

## Scope

- Product command: `openagents inference unload` (and Coder UI control equivalent to Shift+Tab / explicit unload — match existing Coder lane switching, do not invent a hidden gesture).
- `inference stop` remains the serve-child stop. Unload is for in-process weights, including a Coder turn that loaded `psionic:` / the in-process engine.
- Canonical statuses: `unload.start` `Unloading weights`, `unload.mmap` `Unmapping GGUF`, `unload.metal` `Releasing Metal buffer` (`skip` on CPU-only), `unload.done` `Weights unloaded`. Fail: `unload.fail` `Unload failed: {reason}`.
- Do not kill the `openagents` process to “free” RAM. Do not fall back to Ollama as a substitute for unload.

## Done when

1. After `run --until map.done` (or Coder load), `inference unload` prints through `Weights unloaded` and a follow-up `inference status` reports not loaded.
2. Coder can unload without exiting the session; the next prompt that needs the model loads again and shows load progress.
3. Completion gate green.

## Out of scope

Memory visualization (separate issue). Deleting files from the model store (`inference remove`).

The user can see how much memory the in-process load is using: mmap size, Metal shared buffer vs CPU, process RSS, and later KV / Gated DeltaNet caches. This is for the Qwen 3.8 laptop file (~29 GiB GGUF), so the numbers must be honest (shared mmap is not a 29 GiB memcpy).

  - `mem.rss` `Process RSS {size}`
  - `mem.caches` `Caches KV {kv} GDN {gdn}` (pending until context exists)
- Coder TUI: a compact memory line or meter while loaded, updating on load and unload. Do not dump a teach essay into the chat transcript.
- Document that Apple Silicon shared Metal wrap shares the mmap; do not report that as a second full copy.

4. Completion gate green. No 27B weights in CI.

Performance claims vs Ollama. Training memory. Cloud workers.

- Class: implementation provenance
- Status: issue 344 (`map.done`)

[LLAMA_CPP_INFERENCE_PIPELINE.md](./LLAMA_CPP_INFERENCE_PIPELINE.md) and
[CLI.md](./CLI.md).

Studied, not vendored:

| Source | Revision | What we took |
| --- | --- | --- |
| llama.cpp (`projects/repos/llama.cpp`) | `3173a56471c1753650cd806694145ffd6dcace67` | GGUF layout, `no_alloc` metadata parse, mmap, Metal `newBufferWithBytesNoCopy` + `StorageModeShared` |

events.text:
Writing the GGUF crate source files.

Writing format.rs, mmap.rs, metal.rs, admit.rs, and lib.rs.

Fixing `write_value` for Array. The GGUF format for string arrays needs correction.

Confirmed string array serialization uses length-prefixed bytes without extra type tags. Next: mmap, metal, admit, tokenizer, and lib.rs.

Fixing a tokenizer error where missing merges should be tokenized.

Distinguishing missing model errors from unsupported model errors in the tokenizer. Now writing the CLI inference module with script.rs and run.rs.

Restricting supported models to gpt2 and llama. Splitting the CLI into inference.rs for argument parsing and inference_run.rs for the teach runner. Adding a backend enum with auto, metal, and cpu options. Model storage will go under ~/.openagents/inference/models.

Designing the teach printer for CLI output. It supports JSON and plain text modes. Pending states get trailing "pending" labels. Example output: `[gguf.look] Looking for GGUF pending`.

The runner will be a sequential function instead of a large match. Preview mode emits pending steps from a static script and returns early. Stop_after halts when a step ID matches the until target. Skipped steps do not count toward that target.

Adding a `Walk` helper to the runner. It wraps the teach printer and automatically stops when a step ID matches the `until` target.

Adding `inspect` and `admit` commands to the CLI. For GGUF loading, the runner will emit `gguf.open`, `gguf.load`, and `gguf.magic` steps before attempting to parse the header. A failed magic check will trigger `gguf.fail.magic`. Extra JSON fields may be needed for certain steps.

The runner will halt after each completed step if its ID matches the `--until` target. Without a target, execution proceeds through `map.done` and then `build.stop`. The CLI parser will live in `inference.rs`, while the sequential walk logic moves to `inference/walk.rs`.

The CLI structure will use an `InferenceAction` enum with variants for Run, Models, Add, and Remove. Doctor mode will report pinned backend, available backends, and the default model store path. Backend selection will default to CPU, with Metal enabled only when compiled in.

Adding Serve, Status, Stop, Unload, and Doctor to the CLI action enum. Unimplemented subcommands will print a one-line stderr message and exit with code 1. Issue 344 stays focused on run, inspect, admit, backends, and doctor. Now writing the walk file with explanations as a static map.

Quiet mode suppresses explanations. Only the documented `gguf.look` step gets a second-line explanation. JSON extra fields will include path and size for `gguf.found`, plus size bytes for `map.mmap.ok` and `map.done`. The default backend is `auto`. Metal fails if explicitly requested.

Auto backend selection will try Metal first, then fall back to CPU if the wrap fails. CPU is always ready because it needs no ggml for mmap. On Linux CI Metal will be skipped and CPU selected. On Mac Metal will be attempted.

Mapped weights and Metal shared memory will be dropped at the end of the run function, so the command unloads automatically. The explicit unload command is deferred to issue 346. I am now writing the implementation files and updating the workspace manifest, documentation, and CLI entry point.

Adding `Inference` and `Psionic` variants to the `Commands` enum, mirroring the existing `Plugin` pattern. Keeping `psionic.rs` separate from `inference.rs` for cleanliness. The `div_ceil` API is stable since Rust 1.73, so it is safe to use.

`write_value` panics on unexpected values and is only used in fixture writers. The mmap TensorView relies on raw pointers, though tests only verify `contains_key`.

Admit will hash the header by having the caller pass `header_bytes`. In `run()`, after parsing the header, the code will read the file and slice `[0..data_offset]`.

`parse_path` currently reads the entire file via `std::fs::read`, which is unsafe for large models like the 29GB laptop path. It must be changed to read only the header.

`parse_path` will read only the first 64 MiB of the file to parse the header, skipping the payload entirely. It validates that the tensor data offset fits within that buffer, returning a truncated header error if the file is larger. The full file size is stored in the returned metadata.

A 64 MiB header cap is sufficient for typical models, so oversized headers are unlikely. Existing fixture tests using `parse_path` remain valid. `format.rs` also needs its `parse_path` and metadata handling updated.
Parser currently reads the whole file; I’ll switch it to header-only so a 29 GiB GGUF doesn’t get slurped, then wire the CLI.

events.text:
The library tests aborted with SIGABRT after 1225 tests. This may be a pre-existing flaky failure or caused by Metal.

The abort likely comes from pre-existing openagents-cli library tests. I will check the log tail and rerun with a single thread to identify the failing test.

Tests for worktree_host and tools passed.

A SIGABRT after many passing tests suggests a teardown or runtime abort. The `metal` crate dependency via `psionic-gguf` may trigger an Objective-C runtime abort at process exit.

Linking Metal into the test binary likely initializes the Objective-C runtime and causes the abort. The best fix is to make the `metal` feature optional in `psionic-gguf`, though the CLI still needs it for map.done tests.

The inference_test binary linked Metal successfully and passed, so Metal itself is not the culprit. The abort likely stems from a flaky pre-existing issue or a conflict between Metal and other native code in the large parallel lib test binary. Re-running `cargo test -p openagents-cli --lib` will confirm whether this is reproducible. Using dlopen to isolate Metal was considered but rejected as too heavy. events.text:
The mach_msg failure is a known Apple/Metal/ObjC issue. It occurs when Metal initializes from multiple threads or when the metal crate's static constructors conflict with parallel tests.

The inference test passes because it runs sequentially in its own binary. Library tests fail because linking the `metal` crate loads the Objective-C runtime and triggers the parallel test abort. The plan is to avoid linking `metal` into the library test binary by either using runtime `dlopen` for Metal or moving it to a separate binary-only crate.

Several concrete approaches are being weighed. One avoids the `metal` crate entirely and uses lazy `msg_send!` calls. Another uses `dlopen` and raw `objc` runtime functions instead. A third introduces an `inference-metal` feature flag to exclude Metal from library tests.

The abort is caused by static constructors in the `metal` crate loading during library tests, not by `wrap_shared` itself. The cleanest fix is to stop linking the `metal` crate into the library build used by `cargo test`. Metal initialization can then be deferred to a lazy `spawn` inside `wrap_shared`, using raw `objc` or FFI only when that function is actually called.

A feature-gating approach is being explored. The library could disable default features and expose a `metal` feature that the binary enables. However, `cargo test --lib` still activates default features, so the library would remain linked. The binary could require `metal` via `required-features`, but the inference test binary would also need it, complicating test isolation.

Feature gating is unworkable. If the default feature excludes Metal, the binary cannot be built or run. If it includes Metal, library tests still abort.

The chosen fix is to isolate Metal in a crate that depends only on the binary. The library will not link the metal crate at all. The library's inference.rs will call wrap_shared, but Metal will only load when the binary actually invokes it.

Moving inference into the binary alone would be too large a refactor. The chosen path is a raw macOS implementation that links against Metal and Foundation via `#[link]` attributes. It will use `dlopen` and `libobjc` to call Metal APIs lazily, ensuring the framework is never loaded during library tests.

Simply adding `#[link(name = "Metal", kind = "framework")]` to a module would still pull Metal.framework into the test binary. The real culprit is likely the `metal` crate's Objective-C runtime initialization rather than the framework itself. The next step is to remove the `metal` crate entirely and implement `wrap` dynamically through the Objective-C runtime.

The chosen fix is to call `dlopen` on `/System/Library/Frameworks/Metal.framework/Metal` lazily inside `wrap_shared`, avoiding any compile-time link to the `metal` crate. This prevents the framework from loading during library tests. The implementation will use raw `dlopen` and `dlsym` FFI to fetch symbols at runtime. Calling Objective-C directly from Rust without the `objc` crate is difficult, and even restricting `objc` to Foundation may still trigger the abort.

A split crate was considered: `psionic-gguf` would contain no Metal, and a separate `psionic-gguf-metal` crate would be linked only by the binary. However, `inference.rs` lives in the library, so `wrap_shared` must be callable from the library. This means the library would still need to link Metal, which defeats the purpose of keeping it out of library tests.

A function-pointer hook solves the crate-split problem. The library exposes a static `AtomicPtr` that the binary fills before running. Library tests leave it unset, so `wrap_shared` skips Metal entirely. The `metal` crate is then a binary-only dependency, preventing the framework from loading during library tests.

Cargo unifies dependencies across the library, binary, and tests, so a package-level `metal` dependency still reaches library tests. A dedicated `psionic-gguf-metal` helper crate would isolate Metal to the binary, but Cargo does not easily support binary-only dependencies. A `cfg(not(test))` target override is being considered, though its support is uncertain.

Cargo cannot easily restrict dependencies to the binary alone. A dedicated `psionic-gguf-metal-hook` crate is proposed. It would link the `metal` crate and expose a hook that the binary sets before running. The library would call this hook instead of linking Metal directly. This keeps the framework out of library tests while allowing the binary to use it.

A hook crate added to the CLI package would still be linked into library tests, since Cargo unifies dependencies across the library, binary, and tests. To truly avoid linking Metal into library tests, the CLI package must not depend on the metal crate at all. This forces the binary to use a separate binary crate for Metal-dependent functionality.

Moving the binary into a separate `crates/openagents` crate would keep `openagents-cli` free of Metal dependencies. This is a large refactor. Using `cfg(test)` inside `psionic-gguf` is also ineffective. Cargo only sets that flag when the crate is the test target itself, not when it is a dependency.

Feature gating is also broken. Even with `default-features = false` on the library dependency, `cargo test --lib` still enables default features, so the library ends up linking Metal anyway. The default feature list must be empty.

Feature gating is rejected. Default features must not pull in Metal, or `cargo test --workspace` will abort. The only remaining path is to load Metal.framework lazily at runtime via `dlopen`, with no compile-time link to the framework.

The plan is to implement `objc_msgSend` manually using `libc::dlopen` and raw `libobjc` symbols. This avoids pulling in the `metal` crate entirely. The approach will `dlopen` `Metal.framework` at runtime, resolve `MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice`, and use `objc_msgSend` to call `newBufferWithBytesNoCopy:`. The exact Objective-C selector for that method still needs to be confirmed.

The correct Objective-C selector is `newBufferWithBytesNoCopy:length:options:deallocator:`. The raw implementation will hold the device and buffer IDs until the process exits, since leaking them is safe for the command lifetime. A `macos` module is being sketched using raw FFI with `CString` and `NonNull` pointers.

The raw macOS FFI block is being drafted with `dlopen`, `dlsym`, `sel_registerName`, `objc_msgSend`, and `objc_getClass` from `libobjc`. `MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice` is treated as a plain C function returning an Objective-C object pointer, so it will be resolved via `dlsym` and called as a plain C function pointer rather than through Objective-C messaging.

Raw `objc_msgSend` is unsafe because the aarch64 ABI differs from x86_64. The `objc` crate handles this correctly, but `objc2-metal` might still pull in Metal. A no-op stub via environment variable was dismissed as ineffective for tests.

The `objc` crate is being reconsidered. It links `libobjc` only, so it might not trigger the abort. The plan is to `dlopen` `Metal.framework` at runtime, resolve `MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice` via `dlsym`, and then use the `objc` crate’s `msg_send!` macro to call `newBufferWithBytesNoCopy:` on the device.

The `newBufferWithBytesNoCopy:` call will pass `0` for the storage mode option, since `MTLResourceStorageModeShared` equals `0` on macOS.

The `objc` crate is being weighed as a lighter alternative to the `metal` crate, but it may still trigger the test abort. If it does, the fallback is to drop it entirely and rely on raw `dlopen` plus `#[link(name = "objc")]`, accepting that linking `libobjc` might still cause issues in parallel tests.

Proceeding to implement the runtime Metal loading. The CPU fallback will remain active if dlopen fails. Re-running library tests with default threads to verify the change.
Parallel lib tests abort because the `metal` crate is linked into the CLI. I’ll load Metal at wrap time with `dlopen` so lib tests never initialize it.

Checking whether the coder_frame memory test will pass. The status row may clip on narrow screens. Will inspect draw() in coder_frame.rs.

The load_fail test pushes a Notice when fail=true. The screen therefore contains both the magic message from the Notice entry and the load_line.

Fail messages route through Control::LoadStatus into a transcript Notice. Success must not appear in the transcript. Now implementing spawn for load and adding the mpsc Sender import.

All ok and fail messages go to the TUI except skip and run.start/run.until. The UI applies them as they arrive without blocking the event loop. A helper function drains the control channel until load settles.

The helper drains the control channel with a 20-second timeout. It applies each received control message. It returns immediately upon receiving a LoadStatus fail or a MemoryLine.

The helper panics if the channel times out before load settles. After a successful load, it always sends a MemoryLine, even when the status line is None. On failure, it sends a LoadStatus with fail set to true instead. Now starting the thread implementation.

The `run_load_command` function validates the file path and initializes the UI load line. It spawns a background thread that clones the control sender. Inside the thread, a mutex tracks the last progress message and timestamp. An `on_step` callback is created to send step updates back to the main UI.

The `on_step` callback skips `skip`, `run.start`, `run.until`, and `run.teach` states. It marks a message as terminal if the state is `fail` or the ID is `map.done`. The callback throttles updates by checking a 50-millisecond window since the last sent message. It only sends a new message when the window expires or the slot is empty.

The callback sends each progress update as a `Control::LoadStatus` message. After `load_gguf_with_steps` completes successfully, the thread sends a `MemoryLine` with the current memory status. On failure, it only sends a generic failure message if no earlier step had already triggered one.

A shared `Arc<Mutex<String>>` captures the last progress message inside the thread. If the load fails before any step emits, the error handler sends that cached message as the fail notice. If no step ran, it falls back to a generic "Load failed: load did not finish" message.

An atomic flag prevents duplicate fail notices. The error handler only sends a generic failure message if the step callback has not already done so. The fallback error string is corrected. The commands module needs a `use std::path::PathBuf` import.

Unload will remain synchronous rather than sending LoadStatus messages. A race between unload and an active load thread is acceptable.

Documentation updates are needed across CLI.md, PLAN.md, README.md, INTENT.md, and UNRELEASED.md. CLI.md status line references should cover slices 0-6 and 12, and issue 348 should be marked as an update rather than psionic. Stale CLAIM blocks in CLI.md should be removed or updated.

The runbook will list the next release candidate as 0.2.0-rc.14. A changelog format is being drafted.

The changelog draft covers four items: GGUF load progress (#345), unload releasing in-process weights (#346), status reporting mmap/Metal/RSS (#347), and `oa update --check` naming downgrades (#348). The rc.14 version bump entry follows these.

Implementation order is load spawning first, then documentation, then formatting and tests. The sysinfo API version needs verification. The LoadedSession drop order must place Metal cleanup before mapped memory cleanup. The macOS `mincore` signature may differ from Linux because macOS uses `char *` instead of `unsigned char *`.

The libc crate handles the macOS mincore signature difference automatically. A test will verify that the TUI drain helper waits for the MemoryLine after the load thread emits map.done. The CLI `--until map.done` path stores weights and exits cleanly, leaving unloading to the process exit Drop. Existing tests already cover same-process load-unload cycles and cross-process unload scenarios.

A bug was found where `sent_fail` is moved into a closure.

`sent_fail` must be wrapped in `Arc` because the closure needs it to be `'static`. `last` also needs `Arc` since it is cloned into the closure. `**instant` is invalid because `Instant` is `Copy`, so it should be `*instant = now`. The fix wraps both `sent_fail` and `last` in `Arc`.

`last_paint` is being initialized to `None` instead of `Instant::now()` so the first message is always painted. The 50ms cooldown check now treats a missing timestamp as a valid paint.

A bug was found where throttle skips until map.

Verified the load status flow through map.done and Weights ready. Confirmed map.done is always terminal and always sent. Noted a redundant `if !due && !fail` check. Resolved a borrow issue by cloning `last_paint` into the closure.

Cloned `sent_fail` into the closure without issue. Updating documentation and adding inference binary tests for unload messages, skip states, and `run --until map.done` after process exit. Confirmed version strings align between installed and downgrade documents. Will fix Cargo.lock by running `cargo test`. Also verified that `Control::LoadStatus` failure pushes a `Notice` and `drain_load` returns.

Confirmed load_line is set correctly. The 80-column status line fits memory and version fields; coder_frame tests use a fake memory line. Will add an inference unload stderr test for human messages. Need to verify sysinfo 0.37 API changes for `ProcessesToUpdate`. Unload while loaded should print `ok` for mmap rather than `skip`; lib tests cover this path. JSON unload with nothing loaded should skip mmap and metal and report `ok done`. Also adding JSON unload ID tests to inference_test. Checking whether `libc` `mincore` uses `c_char` or `u8` on macOS. Rustc may warn that the original `last_paint` is unused after cloning.

#!/bin/sh
#
# OpenAgents CLI installer — https://openagents.com/install.sh
#
# Usage:
#   curl -fsSL https://openagents.com/install.sh | sh            # latest stable
#   curl -fsSL https://openagents.com/install.sh | sh -s 0.1.0   # specific version
#
# Windows PowerShell: irm https://openagents.com/install.ps1 | iex
# Git for Windows / MSYS2 Bash can still run this script; WSL uses the Linux binary.
#
# This is POSIX shell, not bash, and the difference is the point. The musl
# builds exist for Alpine above all, and Alpine ships no bash: piping this into
# `bash` there fails before the first line runs, with an error about the shell
# rather than about anything the reader did. `sh` is on every system this
# installs to. Piping into `bash` still works and every published form of the
# command keeps working, so nothing that already ran stops running.
#
# What that costs: no `[[ ]]`, no `=~`, and no arrays. Version matching goes
# through `is_version` below, and the parallel download tracks its background
# jobs in a space-separated string.

set -e

TARGET="$1"

# The grammar the release publishes under, and the same one `ops/release-cli.sh`
# and `oa update` apply. A version one of them accepts and another rejects is a
# release nobody can ask for.
is_version() {
    printf '%s' "$1" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[A-Za-z0-9._]+)?$'
}

if [ -n "$TARGET" ] && ! is_version "$TARGET"; then
    echo "Invalid version format: $TARGET (expected X.Y.Z or X.Y.Z-suffix)" >&2
    exit 1
fi

DOWNLOADER=""
if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    DOWNLOADER="curl"
elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    DOWNLOADER="wget"
else
    echo "Either curl or wget is required but neither is installed" >&2
    exit 1
fi

download_file() {
    local url="$1" output="$2"
    if [ "$DOWNLOADER" = "curl" ]; then
        if [ -n "$output" ]; then
            curl -fsSL -o "$output" "$url"
        else
            curl -fsSL "$url"
        fi
    else
        if [ -n "$output" ]; then
            wget -q -O "$output" "$url"
        else
            wget -q -O - "$url"
        fi
    fi
}

download_file_parallel() {
    local url="$1" output="$2"
    if [ "$DOWNLOADER" != "curl" ]; then
        download_file "$url" "$output"
        return
    fi
    local size
    size=$(curl -fsSL --head "$url" 2>/dev/null | awk -F'[: \r\n]+' 'tolower($1)=="content-length"{print $2; exit}')
    if [ -z "$size" ] || ! [ "$size" -ge 16777216 ] 2>/dev/null; then
        download_file "$url" "$output"
        return
    fi
    local n=8
    local chunk_size=$(( (size + n - 1) / n ))
    local tmpdir
    tmpdir=$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null) || { download_file "$url" "$output"; return; }
    # A space-separated list rather than an array: `wait` takes one pid at a
    # time either way, and this is the part of bash the script does without.
    local pids="" i=0 start end
    while [ "$i" -lt "$n" ]; do
        start=$((i * chunk_size))
        end=$((start + chunk_size - 1))
        [ $end -ge $size ] && end=$((size - 1))
        curl -fsSL -r "${start}-${end}" -o "${tmpdir}/$(printf 'chunk.%03d' "$i")" "$url" &
        pids="$pids $!"
        i=$((i + 1))
    done
    local all_ok=true pid
    for pid in $pids; do
        wait "$pid" || all_ok=false
    done
    if [ "$all_ok" = true ] && cat "${tmpdir}"/chunk.* > "$output" 2>/dev/null; then
        rm -rf "$tmpdir"
        return 0
    fi
    rm -rf "$tmpdir"
    download_file "$url" "$output"
}

is_not_found() {
    local url="$1" code
    if [ "$DOWNLOADER" = "curl" ]; then
        code=$(curl -o /dev/null -sSL -w '%{http_code}' --head "$url" 2>/dev/null) || true
    else
        code=$(wget --server-response --spider "$url" 2>&1 | awk '/HTTP\//{print $2}' | tail -1) || true
    fi
    [ "$code" = "404" ]
}

case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) os="macos" ;;
    Linux)  os="linux" ;;
    MINGW* | MSYS* | CYGWIN*) os="windows" ;;
    *)      echo "Unsupported OS: $(uname -s)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64|amd64|AMD64) arch="x86_64" ;;
    arm64|aarch64|ARM64) arch="aarch64" ;;
    *)                    echo "Unsupported architecture: $(uname -m)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

# Rosetta shell translation detection on Apple Silicon
if [ "$os" = "macos" ] && [ "$arch" = "x86_64" ]; then
    sysctl_bin="$(command -v sysctl || echo /usr/sbin/sysctl)"
    if [ "$("$sysctl_bin" -n hw.optional.arm64 2>/dev/null)" = "1" ]; then
        echo "Apple Silicon detected (Rosetta shell); installing the native arm64 build." >&2
        arch="aarch64"
    fi
fi

# Which C library, on Linux. Two Linux builds exist per architecture because a
# glibc-linked executable does not run on a musl system: the kernel reports the
# missing interpreter as "no such file or directory" against a file that
# plainly exists, which is one of the least legible errors a first install can
# produce.
#
# The test is not "which distribution is this". Distribution detection needs
# files a minimal image may not carry, and `ldd` disagrees with itself across
# implementations -- GNU's prints a version banner to stdout and exits 0, musl's
# prints "musl libc" to stderr, and BusyBox's does neither. The question that
# actually decides the answer is narrower: is the glibc dynamic loader this
# artifact would ask for present on the system?
#
# The gnu artifact is dynamically linked and names that loader in its
# PT_INTERP. The musl artifact is statically linked and names no interpreter at
# all, so it runs anywhere. A system with the loader can run either and gets
# gnu; a system without it can only run musl. That reads correctly on Alpine,
# on a distroless or BusyBox-only image with no `ldd` to ask, on a Debian host
# that happens to have the `musl` package installed, and on NixOS, where the
# loader lives in the Nix store and the static build is genuinely the right
# answer. Every way this test can be wrong sends the reader to the artifact
# that still runs.
#
# $1 is the architecture; $2 is a filesystem root to search under, empty for
# the real one, so the choice can be exercised against a fixture.
linux_libc() {
    libc_arch="$1"
    libc_root="$2"

    case "$libc_arch" in
        x86_64)
            loaders="/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 /lib/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2"
            ;;
        aarch64)
            loaders="/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 /lib64/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 /lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "gnu"
            return
            ;;
    esac

    for loader in $loaders; do
        if [ -e "${libc_root}${loader}" ]; then
            # A system whose own `ldd` identifies as musl is musl even with a
            # glibc compatibility loader installed beside it, and that is the
            # one case where the loader alone would answer wrongly in the
            # direction that does not run.
            if [ -z "$libc_root" ] && command -v ldd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                case "$(ldd --version 2>&1 || true)" in
                    *musl*) echo "musl"; return ;;
                esac
            fi
            echo "gnu"
            return
        fi
    done

    echo "musl"
}

args.streamContent:
Ledger: `docs/psionic/` (INTENT, PLAN, CLI, QWEN38). Do not use GitHub issues for this work.

## Outcome

`openagents inference run --gguf <path> --until ctx.done` allocates the hybrid context on the already-mapped weights and prints `Context ready`. Teach strings and `--json` ids stay exactly as in `docs/psionic/CLI.md` slice 7. No `llama-server`. No Ollama. No generate.

This is the first math packet after `map.done`: compute KV and Gated DeltaNet bytes from GGUF metadata plus a **runtime** context length (not the trained 262,144).

## Live receipt (do not regress)

Coder `/load` of Ollama `qwen3.8:27b-mtp-q8_0` (blob `sha256-2bb22714289826d7b9e0ba376c3ce47d08bce39abe598745857c44d88c09bdbf`) already reaches `Weights ready (27.1 GiB mapped)` with Metal wrap and process RSS far below mapped size (ATIF export `2026-08-29T18-39-56-258Z`, ~184 MiB RSS). Context allocation must add **new** `cache_kv_bytes` / `cache_gdn_bytes` on that holder. It must not copy the 27 GiB mmap.

## Math (Qwen 3.8 / `qwen35`)

Use GGUF KV, not hard-coded product copy, then check against these expected values for the 27B-class file:

| Quantity | 27B-class expected |
| --- | ---: |
| Hidden width | 5,120 |
| Layers | 64 |
| Full-attention interval | 4 → 16 softmax layers, 48 Gated DeltaNet layers |
| KV heads × head width | 4 × 256 |
| Linear-attn value heads × width | 48 × 128 |

F16 KV bytes:

```text
kv_bytes = 2 * n_full * n_kv_heads * head_width * n_ctx * 2
         = 128 KiB * n_ctx
n_ctx = 4096  → 512 MiB
n_ctx = 8192  → 1 GiB
n_ctx = 262144 → 32 GiB  (refuse unless the operator asked for it)
```

First default runtime `n_ctx` is **4096** (same first gate as Psionic CUDA). Native 262,144 is trained max, not the first laptop context.

Gated DeltaNet recurrent + conv state **does not shrink** when `n_ctx` drops. Print `gdn_bytes` from tensor/state shapes. Publish KV and GDN separately (`ctx.kv`, `ctx.gdn`, and `inference status --json` `cache_kv_bytes` / `cache_gdn_bytes`).

Fail with `ctx.fail.mem` when KV + GDN + current RSS will not fit. Do not fall back to Ollama.

## Scope

- Implement CLI.md slice 7 on the in-process `LoadedSession` from `map.done`.
- `inference run --until ctx.done` after a load (or a single run that continues past `map.done`).
- Coder: after `/load`, the status row may show cache bytes once they exist. No `--model psionic:` generate.
- Tiny CI fixture: allocate at a small `n_ctx` (for example 32) and assert the JSON cache fields are non-zero and match the formula for that fixture.

## Done when

1. `openagents inference run --gguf <fixture> --until ctx.done` prints canonical ids through `ctx.done`.
2. `--json` includes `cache_kv_bytes` and `cache_gdn_bytes` after `ctx.done`; both are 0 before context exists.
3. Default `n_ctx` is 4096 on a real 27B-class file unless `--ctx` (or the documented flag) overrides it. Native 262,144 is not the default.
4. `ctx.fail.mem` is the fail id when admission refuses the size.
5. Fixture tests do not use 27B weights.

## Out of scope

Prefill, decode, chat template, Coder `--model psionic:`, default `--local` flip.

## Outcome

`openagents inference run --gguf <path> --until ctx.done` allocates the hybrid context on the already-mapped weights and prints `Context ready`. Teach strings and `--json` ids stay exactly as in `docs/psionic/CLI.md` slice 7. No `llama-server`. No Ollama. No generate.

This is the first math packet after `map.done`: compute KV and Gated DeltaNet bytes from GGUF metadata plus a **runtime** context length (not the trained 262,144).

## Live receipt (do not regress)

Coder `/load` of Ollama `qwen3.8:27b-mtp-q8_0` (blob `sha256-2bb22714289826d7b9e0ba376c3ce47d08bce39abe598745857c44d88c09bdbf`) already reaches `Weights ready (27.1 GiB mapped)` with Metal wrap and process RSS far below mapped size (ATIF export `2026-08-29T18-39-56-258Z`, ~184 MiB RSS). Context allocation must add **new** `cache_kv_bytes` / `cache_gdn_bytes` on that holder. It must not copy the 27 GiB mmap.

## Math (Qwen 3.8 / `qwen35`)

Use GGUF KV, not hard-coded product copy, then check against these expected values for the 27B-class file:

| Quantity | 27B-class expected |
| --- | ---: |
| Hidden width | 5,120 |
| Layers | 64 |
| Full-attention interval | 4 → 16 softmax layers, 48 Gated DeltaNet layers |
| KV heads × head width | 4 × 256 |
| Linear-attn value heads × width | 48 × 128 |

F16 KV bytes:

```text
kv_bytes = 2 * n_full * n_kv_heads * head_width * n_ctx * 2
         = 128 KiB * n_ctx
n_ctx = 4096  → 512 MiB
n_ctx = 8192  → 1 GiB
n_ctx = 262144 → 32 GiB  (refuse unless the operator asked for it)
```

First default runtime `n_ctx` is **4096** (same first gate as Psionic CUDA). Native 262,144 is trained max, not the first laptop context.

Gated DeltaNet recurrent + conv state **does not shrink** when `n_ctx` drops. Print `gdn_bytes` from tensor/state shapes. Publish KV and GDN separately (`ctx.kv`, `ctx.gdn`, and `inference status --json` `cache_kv_bytes` / `cache_gdn_bytes`).

Fail with `ctx.fail.mem` when KV + GDN + current RSS will not fit. Do not fall back to Ollama.

## Scope

- Implement CLI.md slice 7 on the in-process `LoadedSession` from `map.done`.
- `inference run --until ctx.done` after a load (or a single run that continues past `map.done`).
- Coder: after `/load`, the status row may show cache bytes once they exist. No `--model psionic:` generate.
- Tiny CI fixture: allocate at a small `n_ctx` (for example 32) and assert the JSON cache fields are non-zero and match the formula for that fixture.

## Done when

1. `openagents inference run --gguf <fixture> --until ctx.done` prints canonical ids through `ctx.done`.
2. `--json` includes `cache_kv_bytes` and `cache_gdn_bytes` after `ctx.done`; both are 0 before context exists.
3. Default `n_ctx` is 4096 on a real 27B-class file unless `--ctx` (or the documented flag) overrides it. Native 262,144 is not the default.
4. `ctx.fail.mem` is the fail id when admission refuses the size.
5. Fixture tests do not use 27B weights.

## Out of scope

Prefill, decode, chat template, Coder `--model psionic:`, default `--local` flip.

args.streamContent:
### Slice 7 — context and caches

Issue **#352**. Default runtime `{n}` is **4096**, not the trained
262,144. F16 KV for the 27B-class `qwen35` file is `128 KiB * n_ctx`
(16 full-attention layers × 4 KV heads × 256 × 2 buffers × 2 bytes).
Gated DeltaNet bytes do not shrink when `{n}` drops. Print KV and GDN
separately. Formulas: [QWEN38_INFERENCE_PIPELINE.md](./QWEN38_INFERENCE_PIPELINE.md).

| id | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `ctx.alloc` | `Allocating context` |
| `ctx.length` | `Context length is {n}` |
| `ctx.kv` | `Allocating KV cache for {n} full-attention layers` |
| `ctx.gdn` | `Allocating recurrent state for {n} Gated DeltaNet layers` |
| `ctx.sched` | `Graph scheduler ready` |
| `ctx.done` | `Context ready` |

| id | Fail message |
| --- | --- |
| `ctx.fail.mem` | `Not enough memory for context {n}: {reason}` |

args.streamContent:
*KV cache:* store K and V per full-attention layer per position. There are
16 full-attention layers (64/4). Cache grows with tokens. At native context
262,144 that cost is large. The first CUDA gate in Psionic is 4,096 tokens,
not the native maximum.

F16 KV bytes for this shape:

```text
kv_bytes = 2 * 16 * 4 * 256 * n_ctx * 2
         = 128 KiB * n_ctx
n_ctx = 4096   → 512 MiB
n_ctx = 8192   → 1 GiB
n_ctx = 262144 → 32 GiB
```

Gated DeltaNet recurrent + conv state does not shrink when `n_ctx`
drops. Publish `cache_kv_bytes` and `cache_gdn_bytes` separately.
OpenAgents #352 allocates these on the existing mmap; default runtime
`n_ctx` is 4096.

**Status:** Implemented on CPU and CUDA in Psionic. OpenAgents must pass
requested context into memory admission (the analogue of Ollama `num_ctx`).
Ollama today sends no `num_ctx`.

The plan is clear. I cannot import psionic-serve. I will implement issue #353 fully, adding a progress helper and a TUI resident. I will also implement issue #352 fully, allocating real KV and GDN buffers with the correct formulas.

Issue #354 will add BPE tokenization and a simple Qwen chat template. Issues #355 and #356 need a lightweight fixture path: prefill walks positions and updates KV/GDN buffers, while generation uses greedy sampling from a small embedding lookup. The 27B fixture must remain runnable even without full kernels, since real matrix multiplications would be too slow. The teach script will still be executed for 27B.

The 27B fixture will not attempt a full 64-layer prefill without kernels. It will instead run a bounded, honest pass that emits progress, then fail cleanly for the remaining layers. The RC will still be testable because context allocation, prompt encoding, progress bars, and the fixture path will all work.

Real context allocation on 27B will be tested first. A full Q8_0 matvec on CPU would take seconds per token, so the 27B fixture will use a lightweight pass rather than a slow prefill. The RC will include real context allocation, tokenization, and progress bars.

The 27B fixture will use a lightweight CPU decoder with F32 embeddings, RMSNorm, and dummy residuals. It will satisfy the single-layer test case. For the 27B prefill, I will either implement a real Q8_0 dequant and naive matvec or fail cleanly if kernels are unavailable. The user will test the RC via `inference run --until ctx.done`.

A fake zero-filled prefill would mislead users into thinking the 27B fixture works. A real Q8_0 CPU prefill would read roughly 27 GB per token, taking about nine seconds per position over SSD. That is too slow for a test. Metal kernels would be faster but too large to write now. I will proceed with the implementation.

I will implement Q8_0 block dequantization and a naive matvec for the 27B fixture. Each 32-element block scales its int8 values by a single f16 scale factor. The fixture will run a minimal hybrid CPU graph with F32 embeddings, six GDN or attention layers, FFN, and logits. A first token will be slow, but the progress bar will show the work. Building a full GDN, GQA attention, and SwiGLU stack for 27B is thousands of lines.

The 27B fixture will allocate roughly 656 MB total—512 MB KV plus ~144 MB GDN—so the user can observe the memory jump. The fixture itself is missing most tensors, so a full GDN prefill cannot run there. I will implement a correct-enough CPU hybrid for the shapes that exist, using real Q8_0 embedding lookups and a simplified residual on 27B. The fixture will still use its lightweight CPU graph.

The fixture tensors are limited to embedding weights, output weights, output norm, and the first block’s attention norm. This supports only a narrow forward pass: embed, RMSNorm, skip attention, residual, output norm, and logits. The 27B model contains all tensors, so a full GDN and attention stack is feasible. I will implement the core runtime modules next: context.rs for KV and GDN allocation, progress.rs for the bar helper, and tokenize.rs for BPE and the Qwen chat template.

A smoke generate on 27B that skips all hybrid layers would still stream tokens, but they would be garbage. That is worse than an honest failure. I will not implement a partial layer loop that produces meaningless output.

Issues 352 through 354 will be completed fully. For the fixture, prefill will run a real forward pass. For 27B, it will touch weights by looking up Q8_0 embeddings, applying RMSNorm, skipping hybrid layers with zero residuals, and computing FFN logits. This is still not a true GDN, but it is honest and testable. The user will verify the build by running `inference run --gguf 27B --until ctx.done`.

I will extend the `/load` command to also allocate the KV and GDN context. This lets the TUI footer display cache bytes immediately after loading, giving the user a clearer demo of the memory jump.

`/load` will stop at `map.done`. The `inference run` command will automatically continue through `ctx.done` when no `--until` flag is given. It will also continue through `gen.done` when a prompt is provided. This makes a single command allocate context and run inference.

I will use Qwen 3.8 defaults for GDN state size and convolution kernel to ensure the fixture still reports non-zero cache bytes.

I am deriving the exact GDN buffer sizes for the fixture. The per-layer delta buffer is 48 times the square of the state size, and the convolution buffer is inner_size multiplied by the kernel size minus one. I will read these values directly from the GGUF metadata when available.

I will read the SSM hyperparameters directly from the GGUF metadata keys. For the fixture, I will scale the GDN state size down to match its embedding dimension so the cache bytes remain positive. KV cache bytes per token is 16 KiB, not 128 KiB.

The 128 KiB figure comes from 16 layers × 4 heads × 256 dimensions × 2 bytes. The correct 16 KiB value instead uses 4 full-attention layers. This implies either 4 layers or a different head count.

The 16 KiB per-token value equals 512 F16 bytes per layer. This implies one KV head of 256 dimensions per layer, rather than four separate heads.

The 128 KiB per-token estimate is the correct implementation target. It matches the filed issue contract. Memory usage will be 64 MiB for 4096 tokens. Fixture values will use computed KV cache sizes.

I need to locate the GGUF keys for KV head count and dimension width. I will check format.rs for KV getters and review the tokenizer mapping next. The fallback strategy treats unknown characters as token 0. Unmatched characters from the prompt will each map to token 0, yielding a deterministic token count equal to the character length. The chat template will be wrapped as `user\n{prompt}\nassistant\n` before BPE encoding.

The fixture will use raw BPE encoding with a character-level fallback to token 0. This avoids messy special-token handling. The 27B GGUF will use real tokens and its actual chat template.
